en.title: Add Numbers Stored as Reversed Digit Linked Lists
en.description:
Two non-negative integers are represented as digit lists with the ones digit first; compute their sum and output it in the same reversed order. The input may contain high-order 0s; this site always removes extra high-order 0s from the result, and zero is output as a single 0.

See the input protocol for this site's supplements to missing ranges and its recovery of typos in the source.
en.input: The input is the length n, n digits, the length m, and m digits, in that order. The original gave no numeric bounds; this site adds 1≤n,m≤100000, with each item in 0..9.
en.output: Output the normalized reversed digits separated by spaces, without the length. Zero is output as a single 0.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 0 5 5 1; 0 1; 0. Verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Add digit by digit while keeping the carry, then remove extra high-order 0s at the end.
